summary: Arbitrary classical psh targets admit decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh sequences on specified curves over countably dense fields, including finite unibranch algebraic normalization. This is a sufficient curve sector, not a characterization.
detailedSummary: Let K be complete, algebraically closed, nontrivially valued, and have a countable dense subset. For smooth proper C, assume its residue field is algebraic over a finite field, or C is P1, or C is Mumford. Every arbitrary classical psh target on an ordinary open subset of C admits ordinary smooth psh approximants decreasing on one fixed ordinary neighborhood, including discontinuities and permitted minus-infinity values. The proof extracts a sequence from Thuillier’s lisse net on a second-countable strictly affinoid domain, applies Wanner Lemma 5.2 separately to its terms, and enforces a quantitative decreasing gap. A finite unibranch normalization permits ordinary smooth descent because each smooth term is constant near the rational preimage of the singularity. Scalar compatibility concerns pullbacks of constructed sequences; general scalar descent, multibranch synchronization, and necessity of the hypotheses remain unresolved.
text:
Claim and published premises. Let K be complete, algebraically closed, nontrivially valued, with a countable dense subset. Let C be smooth proper algebraic, and suppose either the residue field is algebraic over a finite field, C=P1, or C is Mumford. Every arbitrary classical psh u:W→R∪{−∞} on an ordinary open W⊂C^an has, near each point, a decreasing sequence of finite ordinary CLD-smooth psh functions on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. GR arXiv:2506.13548v2, 3.4.2 and 4.1.2, identifies the starting class on connected smooth strictly analytic curves with Thuillier subharmonic functions or the identically −∞ case. Thuillier Theorem 3.4.2 supplies a decreasing net of finite continuous lisse subharmonic functions. Wanner’s standing field assumptions are exactly the field assumptions above except countable density. Her Lemma 5.2, under H_C⊂C∞, uniformly smooths each lisse subharmonic function on a strictly affinoid Y by continuous functions on Y which are ordinary smooth and psh on Y\∂Y. Her Corollary 5.4 verifies H_C⊂C∞ under the three displayed conditions; its own target is finite continuous, so it is not invoked directly for arbitrary u.

Countable extraction. On a second-countable space Z, let continuous f_i decrease as a net to u. For rational q, {u<q}=⋃_i{f_i<q}. Each such open subspace is Lindelöf, so select countably many indices covering it. Enumerate all selected indices over all rational q and recursively choose indices dominating the preceding choice and the next selected index. The resulting terms decrease, remain above u, and eventually lie below every rational q>u(z). This proves pointwise convergence, including u(z)=−∞. The chosen indices need not be cofinal in the original directed set.

Why the countability hypothesis holds here. A strictly affinoid algebra A is a quotient of K〈T1,…,TN〉. Polynomials over a countable dense subring give a countable dense subset A0. For every bounded multiplicative seminorm x, |a(x)|≤||a||, by applying boundedness to powers. Therefore ||a(x)|−|b(x)||≤||a−b|| uniformly in x. All evaluation functions are uniform limits of evaluations from A0. Their rational interval inverse images and finite intersections form a countable base for M(A).

Construction on a fixed neighborhood. Take a relatively compact ordinary open W′ around x inside W and one strictly affinoid neighborhood Y⊂W′ of x. Restrict Thuillier’s net to Y and apply the extraction argument to obtain h_j↓u on Y. Put V=Y\∂Y, an ordinary open neighborhood of x. Apply Wanner Lemma 5.2 to each h_j on this same Y, obtaining a continuous s_j on Y, ordinary smooth and psh on V, with ||s_j−h_j||_Y≤ε_j=2^(−j). Define v_j=s_j+4ε_j. Then h_j+3ε_j≤v_j≤h_j+5ε_j and
v_j−v_(j+1)≥h_j−h_(j+1)+4(ε_j−ε_(j+1))−ε_j−ε_(j+1)≥ε_j/2>0.
Thus v_j↓u on the single fixed V. At a minus-infinity value the upper bound tends to minus infinity. For an identically minus-infinity neighborhood use v_j=−j. Local uniform convergence is asserted only for finite continuous targets, by Dini’s theorem.

Ordinary regularity, positivity, and compatibility. Wanner’s lemma uses ordinary smooth harmonic pieces under H_C⊂C∞ and convex regularized maxima on annuli, with agreement near the gluing boundaries. The positivity conclusion is supplied by that lemma. Adding constants preserves it. The actual saved CD v2 uses ordinary open charts in Proposition 15.1.1(b); its smooth stage is Psh_0, its first decreasing-sequence stage is Psh_1 in Lemma 8.1.4, and smooth pullback is covered by Proposition 8.1.5. These functions have nonnegative d′d″ forms and, on the boundaryless neighborhoods here, positive d′d″[v_j] currents by CD §8.3 and Proposition 8.3.1. Ordinary chart representatives agree because each v_j is one globally defined function on V.

For every analytic extension L/K, the same smooth real chart functions applied to the pulled-back analytic units represent v_j∘π on ordinary opens of V_L. CD Lemma 6.5.1 gives local positive tropical representatives of d′d″v_j. Their pulled-back images remain in the same paralinéaire support, and CD Lemma 1.2.11 preserves their positivity under linear pullback. Thus the scalar pullbacks are ordinary smooth psh. Their gaps remain ≥2^(−j−1), and their pointwise limit is u∘π. No countability of L is required, and no independently constructed sequences must be synchronized.

Unibranch extension. Let D be an integral proper algebraic curve with finite normalization ν:C→D bijective on geometric points, where C satisfies the conditions above. Near a singular point x remove the other finitely many singularities. There is one rational rigid point x′ over x, and ν is an isomorphism elsewhere. The finite closed bijection is a homeomorphism. Pull u back to C and construct the preceding sequence on V′ around x′. Closedness supplies one ordinary N around x with ν^(−1)(N)⊂V′. Descend the sequence by the homeomorphism. Every ordinary smooth function is constant near a rational rigid point: in an ordinary chart, finitely many invertible a_i satisfy |a_i−a_i(x′)|<|a_i(x′)| on a sufficiently small neighborhood, so all |a_i| are constant. Each descended term is consequently constant near x and smooth by the isomorphism elsewhere. Its d′d″ form is zero on the constant neighborhood and nonnegative elsewhere. Global descent preserves its gaps and limit. Scalar pullback then follows from the preceding chart argument. This includes cuspidal proper curves with normalization P1.

Limitations. The field and harmonic-smoothness conditions are sufficient, not proved necessary. Multibranch normalization can give different constant values on different preimages at every stage; limit agreement does not justify descent. No general finite smooth descent or strict scalar descent is claimed. All-domain lisse functions were not identified with strict real-PL functions, and weak smoothness was not substituted for ordinary smoothness.

summary: All arbitrary classical psh targets on saturated products of a permitted curve with proper projective fibres have decreasing ordinary smooth psh approximants. This does not establish regularization of nonsaturated higher-dimensional sheaf germs.
detailedSummary: Under n1’s smooth curve hypotheses, every classical psh function defined on the entire saturated domain U×P^m analytification is constant on each proper fibre. A rational section identifies it with a subharmonic target on U, so n1’s ordinary smooth sequence pulls back on a fixed saturated neighborhood. The starting target need not be continuous, finite, or torus invariant. The conclusion depends on having whole proper fibres in the domain of definition; it does not cover arbitrary targets initially defined on smaller nonsaturated charts.
text:
Let K and the smooth proper curve C satisfy n1, let U⊂C^an be ordinary open, and let X=U×_K(P^m_K)^an with m≥1 and projection p. For every arbitrary classical psh u defined on all of this saturated X, each z∈U has an ordinary neighborhood V such that u|p^(−1)(V) is a decreasing limit of finite ordinary CLD-smooth psh functions on that one fixed ordinary open.

Proof. The fibre over z is (P^m_H(z))^an. GR v2 Proposition 4.2(5,6) makes the restriction of u classical psh there. This fibre is compact, connected, and boundaryless. If the restriction is not identically −∞, upper semicontinuity and compactness give a finite attained maximum M. Its maximum locus is nonempty and closed. GR Theorem 6.1 applies at every point of this locus because the entire fibre is an analytic interior; the locus is therefore open. Connectedness implies that u is constant on the fibre. The identically −∞ case is already constant.

Choose a rational point o of P^m and its section s:U→X. The function w=u∘s is classical psh by analytic pullback, hence subharmonic on the curve, and fibre constancy proves the actual equality u=w∘p, including −∞ values. Apply n1 to w at z. Pull its terms w_j back to w_j∘p on p^(−1)(V). Ordinary smoothness and positive d′d″ forms follow from the proved ordinary chart pullback argument. The same quantitative gaps and pointwise convergence are preserved. In the identically −∞ case use constants −j. The products are boundaryless, so the smooth currents are positive as well.

Each term is globally given by the projection formula. Ordinary chart overlaps therefore agree, and after every analytic extension the formula is exactly w_j,L∘p_L. This proves the asserted scalar compatibility without choosing new approximants over the extension.

Scope. This treats all targets on the specified saturated domains and permits noninvariant, discontinuous, or −∞-valued targets. A target on a nonsaturated affine chart need not extend to whole proper fibres. The fibre maximum argument cannot be applied to it, and no such extension theorem was proved. Consequently this result does not establish the original higher-dimensional local sheaf characterization.

The full proof and this limitation appear in P02.4-argument.md and P02.4-paper.tex; the maximum-principle source proof and exact application checks are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. summary: A classical psh Gauss-boundary spike on a closed disc admits no local continuous sequence when the residue field is uncountable. For this particular spike, countable residue is sufficient via an explicit decreasing ordinary smooth positive-form sequence.
detailedSummary: Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field, set u=A>0 at the Gauss point of the closed unit disc and zero elsewhere. GR’s exact boundary proposition verifies that this USC function is classically psh, including scalar compatibility. Every neighborhood of the Gauss point contains all but finitely many whole residue discs. An uncountable collection of such directions defeats any pointwise continuous sequence on any fixed neighborhood. The obstruction also transfers to higher-dimensional products by an analytic section. When the residue field is countable, enumerated residue representatives and a smooth convex cutoff of j log|∏(T−a_i)| give actual decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh approximants on the entire fixed disc. This equivalence concerns the spike, not every target or a complete boundary characterization.
text:
Let K be complete, algebraically closed, and nontrivially valued. Put D=M(K〈T〉), let η be its Gauss point, and fix A>0. Define u(η)=A and u(x)=0 for x≠η. Since {η} is closed, u is upper semicontinuous. The analytic boundary of D is {η}, and u is zero on Int(D). GR arXiv:2506.13548v2 Proposition 3.5(3), whose literal scalar-compatible proof was checked, says u is subharmonic on D. GR 4.1.2 makes it classical psh. Thus the example belongs to the actual original starting class.

Residue directions. For each α in the residue field choose a representative a_α∈K° and let D_α={|T−a_α|<1}. These nonempty disjoint ordinary open discs partition D\{η}. Indeed, if a point has |T−a_α|=1 for every residue class, factor polynomials over K to see that its polynomial evaluations are the Gauss norms; approximation of Tate series by polynomials makes the point η. The ultrametric inequality gives uniqueness of the residue direction otherwise.

Every ordinary neighborhood of η contains all but finitely many whole D_α. A basic neighborhood uses finitely many Tate-series evaluations. A nonzero normalized series has a nonzero polynomial reduction because its coefficients tend to zero. Away from the finitely many roots of that reduction its absolute value is its Gauss norm throughout the corresponding residue disc. To verify this, translate by a_α: the constant term has full norm, while every nonconstant term multiplied by (T−a_α)^n has smaller norm on that disc. Thus finitely many evaluations exclude only finitely many directions.

Failure for uncountable residue. Suppose finite continuous v_j on an ordinary N containing η converge pointwise to u. Discard finitely many indices so that v_j(η)>3A/4. Continuity gives an ordinary neighborhood N_j⊂N of η with v_j>A/2. Each N_j contains every whole residue disc outside a finite exception set E_j. If the residue field is uncountable, choose α outside the countable union of E_j. At its rigid representative a_α all remaining v_j exceed A/2, contradicting u(a_α)=0. Neither decreasingness nor positivity was needed. In particular D fails P02.4 at its actual analytic boundary.

Higher-dimensional failure. On D×(P^m_K)^an, the projection pullback of u is classical psh by GR Proposition 4.2(6). Any continuous approximating sequence near (η,o), with o rational, restricts along the analytic section D×{o} to such a sequence near η. The preceding contradiction applies. These are good strictly analytic examples in every positive dimension of this product family.

Explicit countable-residue construction. Enumerate the residue field and choose representatives a_1,a_2,… . Choose a nonzero nonnegative smooth bump β supported in (−1,−1/2), and define
c=A/[∫(−t)β(t)dt],  χ(s)=c∫_(−∞)^s(s−t)β(t)dt.
Then χ is smooth, convex, nondecreasing, zero for s≤−1, and χ(0)=A. Put P_j=∏_(i≤j)(T−a_i) and v_j=χ(j log|P_j|), taking value zero at zeros of P_j. Away from zeros this is an ordinary smooth function of the logarithm of an analytic unit. On {|P_j|<exp(−1/j)} it is identically zero, proving ordinary smooth extension at zeros. These ordinary open representations agree on their overlaps.

Writing ℓ=j log|P_j| on the nonzero locus gives d′d″v_j=χ″(ℓ)d′ℓ∧d″ℓ≥0; on the constant neighborhoods it is zero. Thus these are ordinary CLD-smooth stage-zero psh functions. Current positivity is also valid on their boundaryless interiors; no unqualified boundary-current inference from CD §8.3 is made.

All log|T−a_i|≤0 on D. Consequently
(j+1)log|P_(j+1)|−j log|P_j|=∑_(i≤j)log|T−a_i|+(j+1)log|T−a_(j+1)|≤0.
Monotonicity of χ proves v_(j+1)≤v_j, also at zeros. At η every v_j=A. For x≠η choose i with r=|T−a_i|(x)<1. For j≥i, either P_j(x)=0 or j log|P_j(x)|≤j log r→−∞, so v_j(x) is eventually exactly zero. Hence v_j↓u on the entire fixed D.

Every analytic scalar extension preserves the polynomials, ordinary cutoff charts, positive Hessian formula, and decreasing inequalities. The pulled-back sequence converges to u∘π. If the new residue field is uncountable, this target is supported on the entire fibre π^(−1)(η), not just the new Gauss singleton, so there is no contradiction with the obstruction.

Sharpness and limits. Countability of the residue field is necessary and sufficient for this spike to admit the displayed ordinary smooth positive-form sequence. No characterization of all classical psh targets on countable-residue discs follows. This is an actual boundary obstruction, independent of harmonic ordinary-smoothness or residue-genus claims.

Residue-Picard limitation. In Thuillier’s proper geometrically connected semistable type-two setup, H_x/F_x≃Pic^0(C_x)⊗_Z R. GJR Remark 15.10 identifies F with ordinary smooth harmonic functions. A nonzero quotient establishes existence of a harmonic germ that is not ordinary smooth. It does not rule out decreasing ordinary smooth nonharmonic psh approximants. Positive residual genus alone does not imply a nonzero quotient: over an algebraic closure of a finite field, each Jacobian point is defined over some finite field and is torsion. The actual Thuillier PDF contains a stronger sentence asserting finiteness of the entire group; that sentence was not used. The elementary pointwise torsion argument gives the needed conclusion. Neither the positive hypotheses of n1 nor a proposed Picard failure range has been proved sharp.
